item.description:
### Added
- A new Profile now opens on a short setup instead of a sample Project. It shows which Agents Nodex found, lets you sign in or install the ones you want, or add Nodex credits if you'd rather pay as you go, offers the projects you've already used with Codex and Claude Code, and lands on New Chat with a first task ready to send. Nothing is created until you choose it, and `Run setup again` in Settings replays it. - Insights shows what your agents did across this device, and turns it into a card you can share. Open it from the rail to see tokens, models, cost at API list price, messages, how many agents ran at once, tasks finished and Pages written, including Claude Code and Codex history from before you installed Nodex. Reading that history takes one click to allow and keeps only counts on your device. Share makes a Skyline or Receipt image to copy, save or post, with no project names or prompts on it. - Archiving a chat now lets you take it back. A toast appears right away: Undo restores the chat and returns you to it, and View opens your archived chats. - Settings now shows exactly what usage analytics send. Open See what is sent in Settings → General → Privacy to read your random ID and every event waiting or sent since launch. Prompts, code, titles and file paths have no field to travel in. - The Codex usage ring now shows your remaining credits. Hover it to see your balance below the usage windows. When a limit is used up and credits keep you working, the ring turns amber instead of red, and the card says the credits are in use. - You choose which models Nodex can use in Settings → Models. An off model leaves every model menu, and nothing in Nodex can start it. Nodex credits are protected by default: only what you start can spend them, so an Agent on another provider can't start a Nodex subagent unless you allow it, and turning Nodex off means nothing on this computer can spend them. - Account settings now show what each Nodex model costs. Model prices lists input, cache and output prices per million tokens in credits, always current with what the service charges, so you can see what a top-up buys before you pay. - You can add and remove images when you edit a sent message. Its images move into the editor, where you can paste, drop or pick more and remove any of them, so a wrong screenshot no longer means starting over. An image whose file was lost shows as failed, and removing it lets the edit through. - Claude Code chats can now use the built-in Browser, your Chrome, and Computer Use. Ask Claude to open a page, test your local app, or work in a Mac app, and it asks before it runs code or reaches a new site or app. - Nodex now has an iOS and Android app. Drop a thought into the Inbox, start a chat, follow a running chat live, and answer its approvals and questions from your phone. Turn it on and pair a phone in Settings > Mobile. It connects directly to your computer over your local network or a tailnet, encrypted end to end, and captures made offline send when your computer is back. - You can stop an Inbox suggestion that is taking too long. Hover its spinner and click stop: the work ends at once, no more usage is spent, and the message keeps any advice it had or offers Suggest. - You choose the reasoning effort and speed Inbox suggestions run at, in the same model menu new chats use. Until you do, they stay at high on Codex and medium on Claude. - You choose which model titles your chats in Settings → General. Until you pick one, a light model on the chat's own Agent writes the title, such as GPT-6 Luna on Codex and Haiku on Claude Code, so titles cost less on your expensive models. A model you pick receives each chat's first message, and can also title chats on Agents that can't generate text themselves. - A Terminal's tab names the program running in it. The title a program sets replaces the folder name while it runs, unless it only repeats the working directory.
### Changed
- Agent activity now says what happened in plain language, naming the Pages and chats it touched instead of showing IDs. Rows read like `Read Launch plan` or `Updated Launch plan +2 -1`, every Nodex tool has one, and clicking a name opens that Page or chat. Opening a row shows the result for reading, such as the formatted Page or the diff, and hovering a Nodex or MCP tool row reveals an inspector with the exact input, output and record. - OpenCode models now start off, free ones included, so a new chat never lands on a third party's model unless you chose it. Turn them on during setup or in Settings → Models. - You can now search the conversations you import from Codex and Claude Code. Settings → Conversations lists your whole history as soon as it opens: type to find a conversation by title or folder, filter by Agent, folder or import status, and select across several searches before importing. The same field still takes a pasted link or ID, and the list and its import controls now stay on screen together however long your history is. - New chats remember the model you last chose for one, on any Agent. Pick Claude Code, OpenCode or a Nodex model in a new chat and the next one starts there with the same effort and options, instead of going back to Codex. Switching models inside a chat you already started now stays with that chat, so it no longer changes what new chats start on. - Notifications stack at the top of the window. Up to three show at once and fan out when you hover them, hovering pauses their timers, and you can swipe one away. - Usage analytics and crash reports are now on by default, and first launch says so. Nothing is sent until you have had a minute to turn it off in Settings → General → Privacy, and turning usage analytics off takes effect at once and discards anything unsent. `DO_NOT_TRACK` is respected. Session replays stay off unless you enable them, and the separate web analytics setting is gone because Nodex no longer collects web analytics in the app. - Reviewing unsaved edits now shows exactly what they would add to the Page. Word-level changes appear in place, unchanged content folds away, and one sentence says what restoring does or that nothing was lost, so you no longer compare two full copies by eye. Edits that can't be merged can still be copied back with one click, and discarding applies immediately with Undo. - Agent chats now take far less disk space, and their history no longer grows without limit. A store of about 9 GB from a month of heavy use shrank to about 2.5 GB. Nodex keeps a day or two of internal activity instead of all of it, compresses command output, and no longer records hooks that finish with nothing to report. An older store upgrades once, which can pause the first Agent start after updating and a later one for a few minutes. History keeps the first and last 128 KiB of a command's output, and Hooks now appears on a reply only when a hook failed, blocked, stopped or reported something. - Nodex prepaid balances are now counted in credits instead of dollars, at 25 credits to $1. Your balance keeps its value and reads as a whole number, and Top up shows how many credits each amount adds. - The macOS installer is about 30% smaller, so first-time downloads finish sooner, and Nodex uses about 250 MB less disk space. Opening the disk image and copying Nodex to Applications take a little longer on a first install. - The Windows installer is about a fifth smaller, and installing it takes less disk space. - Full macOS updates are about 40% smaller, so updating downloads much less when an incremental update isn't available. - Inbox suggestions no longer wait in line behind each other. Up to five run at once, or as many as 16 if you raise the limit in Settings → Inbox, so a message that takes a while to look into doesn't hold up the ones after it, and every message waiting for advice shows its own spinner instead of only the newest one. - `⌘K` (`Ctrl+K` on Windows and Linux) clears a focused Terminal. It opens the command palette everywhere else.
### Fixed
- Agents now show the HTML pages they make as rendered pages beside the chat. Opening one used to show its source code. An Agent opening the page again reloads the same tab, so you see its edits, and it can still show you the source when you ask. - A chat that continues after a restart can open tabs beside it again. With several windows open, its Agent used to stop and show you nothing; it now uses the window showing that chat. - The marker showing that a chat moved to another Agent now stays visible. It says which Agents the chat moved between and what it carried, and it used to fold away as soon as the reply finished. - Returning a chat to Codex keeps Codex's own conversation. A resume that had already succeeded could be thrown away because its background terminals couldn't be listed, which started a new conversation and pasted the whole history into it. - Fast mode now works on current Codex models. The Fast toggle, `/fast`, the speed setting for new chats, a scheduled task's speed and `speed="fast"` in a prompt's agent config had no effect or failed, because these models name the tier differently. If you turned Fast on earlier, new chats now really run at Fast and use more of your usage; turn it off in the model menu or Settings. - Claude Code chats no longer stop partway through a long tool call. A long script or file could end the reply and kill the command it was running; how much an Agent streams can no longer end a reply. - Chats woken by finished background work no longer end silently after an error. If the Agent stopped during that reply, the chat looked finished until you typed “continue”; now it recovers and carries on like any other reply, on Claude Code, OpenCode and ACP Agents. - Long chats no longer use more memory the longer an Agent runs. A Turn with thousands of messages or file changes now holds only its most recent work in memory, even while it runs and when you are looking elsewhere, and earlier work loads back as you scroll up. - Settings → Data controls now lists every archived chat. Most archived chats used to be missing from it, so they couldn't be found or restored there, and restoring some of the ones it did list failed. - Searching your chats and reading one from another Agent now shows only what you wrote. Page references, selected text and app data sent with a message used to appear there as raw links. - Automatic choices no longer pick a prepaid Nodex model. A subagent that named only a type of Agent, Inbox suggestions, the mobile app and Refine could land on one and spend your credits without you choosing it. - Chats on OpenCode now get a generated title instead of keeping the words of their first message. The same failure also stopped Inbox suggestions and text rewrites on Codex set up by signing in with ChatGPT, and those work now too. - Editing a message no longer loses your conversation when one of its images can't be read. The edit now stops before anything is rewound, keeps your draft open, and says the image can't be read instead of showing a system error. - MCP tool images and rich results now appear in Claude Code chats, both live and in saved conversations. They used to show as raw JSON. - “Allow for this chat” in Claude Code chats now lasts for the whole chat. Claude used to ask again after you pressed Stop, changed models, or restarted Nodex. - Windows updates install reliably while Nodex is running. An update could stop with an error when a Nodex process was exiting at the same moment, or on a busy computer. A failed update now records why. - Quitting Nodex no longer leaves background processes running. An OpenCode server or provider check that was starting as you quit could keep running until the next launch, and windows could log `Runtime Scope closed` errors while closing. - Terminals that Agents start work again in the macOS app. They could fail immediately with `posix_spawnp failed`, because the packaged Agent Runtime looked for its terminal helper in the wrong place. - Inbox suggestions now save when the Agent keeps a message’s existing title. This could previously fail with an internal document error; advice that cannot be saved now explains the problem in plain language. - A busy computer no longer breaks your chats. When CPU and memory were nearly exhausted, opening a chat or the Subagents panel could fail with "Operation timed out after '30s'" and stay failed until you clicked Retry. Nodex now waits for Agent execution to answer and catches up on its own; if that takes too long, a notice says so and offers Restart. - A suggestion that fails on Claude now says why. Claude's own reason, such as a usage limit or an unavailable model, shows beside the message instead of "Claude CLI returned unexpected output format." - Terminal programs keep their colors however Nodex was started. Launching Nodex from an Agent or another terminal could pass along settings such as `NO_COLOR`, which left full-screen programs like lazygit without any color. - Full-screen terminal programs come back intact when you reopen their tab. They return to their own screen and redraw, instead of leaving stale output or receiving stray replies as keyboard input. - Terminal output is no longer lost under heavy load, and programs that move the cursor with bare line feeds draw in the right place. - Pasting into a Terminal on Windows and Linux uses bracketed paste, so a multi-line paste no longer runs line by line in shells that support it.
